questions.stem: Why is the disappearing cross method considered less reliable than using a gas syringe?

options.text: Because the cross experiment is more expensive to set up
Because the gas syringe is simpler to use
Because judging when the cross disappears is subjective and only gives one data point per experiment
Because the cross method cannot be used with acids

questions.explanation: The disappearing cross method is subjective because different observers may disagree on the exact moment the cross is no longer visible. It also only provides a single time measurement per experiment, unlike a gas syringe which gives continuous volume readings over time for a full rate profile.
